proposal.utterance: How should 'sustaining practice' (the practice that sustains an institution over time) be classified in BFO?

entities.label: SustainingPractice
entities.rationale: A sustaining practice is a temporally extended happening — a recurrent pattern of activity (e.g. officials applying norms, citizens complying, courts adjudicating) that unfolds over time and maintains an institution in existence. As something that occurs and has temporal parts, it fits BFO Process (BFO_0000015) best. It is not a continuant because it does not persist by being wholly present at each moment; rather it unfolds. It is not a disposition because it is not merely a capacity but an actual ongoing activity. It is not a generically dependent continuant because it is not an information artifact that can be copied; it is a concrete social process.

relations.rationale: SustainingPractice is a subclass of BFO Process: it is a temporally extended, concrete occurrence that sustains a legal institution.

SustainingPractice is a kind of BehavioralLegalManifestation already in the ontology: both are process-level classes representing concrete behavioral occurrences within a legal context. Subsuming SustainingPractice under BehavioralLegalManifestation avoids duplication and captures the behavioral character of sustaining practices.

A sustaining practice (process) realizes the InstitutionalPersistence quality disposition insofar as the ongoing practice is what makes institutional persistence actual. More precisely, the practice realizes the disposition/capacity for the institution to persist; the domain is a process realizing a realizable. InstitutionalPersistence is currently typed as Quality (BFO_0000019); if it were retyped as a Disposition this relation would be cleaner — flagged as open question.

open_questions: Should SustainingPractice be further distinguished from BehavioralLegalManifestation, or is it a strict subclass? The key differentiator is that SustainingPractice is specifically the recurrent process that keeps an institution in existence over time, whereas BehavioralLegalManifestation may cover any behaviorally manifested legal act.

InstitutionalPersistence is currently typed as Quality (BFO_0000019). Should it be retyped as Disposition (BFO_0000016) so that SustainingPractice can properly 'realize' it via BFO_0000055? A quality is a static property, not a realizable entity; the capacity to persist seems more dispositional.

Is 'sustaining practice' always an aggregate of many individual acts (a process aggregate), or is each individual act itself a sustaining practice? If aggregate, we may want to note that SustainingPractice has parts (BFO_0000051) that are individual process instances.

Should SustainingPractice be linked to LegalInstitution via RO_0000057 (has participant), meaning the institution participates in the sustaining practice? Or is the institution better modeled as the bearer of a quality that the practice realizes?

Is there a distinction between a sustaining practice that is conscious/intentional (officials deliberately applying norms) and one that is habitual/unreflective? If so, we might want subclasses distinguishing intentional from habitual sustaining practices.
proposal.rationale_summary: A 'sustaining practice' — the ongoing activity that keeps a legal institution in existence over time — is best typed as a BFO Process (BFO_0000015) because it is a temporally extended concrete occurrence, not a property that inheres in a bearer and not an information artifact. It unfolds over time and has temporal parts (individual acts of compliance, adjudication, norm-application), which is the hallmark of a BFO occurrent. I propose a new class SustainingPractice as a subclass of BFO_0000015 and, to maximize reuse, also a subclass of the existing working:BehavioralLegalManifestation (already a Process subclass). I add a tentative 'realizes' relation (BFO_0000055) from SustainingPractice to working:InstitutionalPersistence to capture the idea that the practice is what actualizes institutional persistence, though this relation is semantically cleanest if InstitutionalPersistence were a Disposition rather than a Quality — flagged as an open question for the user.
